The test image shows soybean pods with dark brown/purple irregular blotchy lesions covering large portions of the pod surface. Key features:
- Affected part: pods
- Color: dark brown to purple-black irregular blotches
- Pattern: irregular, coalescing spots covering large pod areas
- Some pods show lighter centers within dark lesions

Top candidates: Anthracnose, Cercospora, Phomopsis/Diaporthe, Bacterial_Blight. Let me view reference images.
The Anthracnose reference (bottom right panel) shows a very similar pattern to the test image — green pods with dark brown/black irregular blotches. Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.
None of these match the test image (pod lesions). Let me view more references to meet the minimum requirement and rule out remaining candidates.

I've now viewed 21 reference images. Let me analyze the evidence:

**Test image features:**
- Affected part: green soybean pods
- Dark brown to purple-black, large irregular blotchy lesions covering substantial pod surface area
- Some lighter tan/pinkish areas within darker lesions
- Lesions coalesce across pod surface

**Comparison:**
- **Anthracnose**: Bottom-right panel of the reference shows a green pod with nearly identical dark, irregular blotches — matches best. Description says "brown irregularly shaped spots on stems, pods and petioles."
- **Cercospora**: Primarily leaf purple discoloration — no match
- **Phomopsis/Diaporthe**: Late-season dry pods with circular pycnidia — no match
- **Bacterial_Blight**: Angular spots on leaves with yellow halos — no match
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: Interior pod/seed lesions, not exterior surface blotches
- All root/stem rot diseases (Fusarium, Pythium, Rhizoctonia, etc.): No match

The dark, irregular coalescing blotches on green pods is characteristic of Anthracnose (*Colletotrichum truncatum*), which produces exactly this pattern on pods.
